value.author: orchestrator
value.text: Orchestrator review found a fail-open. Making angle and curly brackets path-continuation characters let a refused path ride behind a permitted prefix. The smuggled forms were: a placeholder home path, then a non-placeholder segment ending in a closing angle bracket, then the root account's ssh directory; a procfs self path, then a curly bracket, then a temp path; a hosted-runner workspace path, then a tilde username path; a Windows placeholder Users path, then a second drive. All of them passed the gate. 9586643 refused them, so this was a regression in the refusal direction. The embedded-identity check only looked for home, Users or a bare drive segment. Fix: hidesHostPathBehindBracket in gate.ts treats a bracket in a non-placeholder segment as the start of a new path, and re-judges the text after it with every host-path rule. Corpus: 4 smuggled-* refuse rows, plus 2 must-allow rows (placeholder in markup, placeholder followed by public procfs). Proof: 20/20 mutations, including the new remove-bracket-smuggle-check (4 refuse flips); the procfs, placeholder and windows-runner expectations were updated for the rows they legitimately flip. Gate tests 134/134; every branch of the new function is exercised.

value.author: pi-github
value.text:
Review round on the public-forms gate (five findings, all fixed on the branch):
1. Major: the bracket-smuggle confirm re-entered the host-path rules, so ~40 repeated procfs-style segments each ending in a delimiter cost about 2^40 confirm calls, and long bracket runs made the loop quadratic with a fresh RegExp per bracket and rule (measured: 415 ms at 16 segments, 5.6 s at 20, 23 s at 22, 934 ms for a 20,000-bracket run; the 40-segment chain did not finish). Rewrote the check as one non-recursive pass that judges only delimiters directly followed by a possible path start, using the non-recursive public-path predicates and sticky rule patterns built once: 1.1 ms for the 40-segment chain, 40 ms for the 20,000-bracket run; a corpus timing test keeps both under 200 ms.
2. Minor: refused roots still passed inside permitted tails. The delimiter set grew from brackets to colon and equals (label/assignment prefixes hide a path the same way), and the embedded-identity list grew to tmp, private, Volumes, mnt, media, srv and root - the last exempt only directly after a procfs numeric or self pid, where procfs exposes the real root entry. The hosted runner's own tmp scratch directory inside its workspace stays allowed (corpus rows both directions). Pinned the two traced refusals as must-refuse rows.
3. Minor: the evidence doc now records the comparison scanner commit and marks which receipts predate the bracket fix.
4. Minor: the README evidence link is now an absolute repository URL instead of a relative link to a doc the package does not ship.
5. Trivial: the no-echo assertion now checks the path-like token of every must-refuse row (all groups) instead of the whole corpus line, and proves it can fail.

value.text: Fifth CodeRabbit round on c589222 (orchestrator, 2026-11-03). Both findings are confirmed and fixed. (1) The delimiter scan's per-segment verdict now uses isHomePlaceholderSegment, so whole env placeholders (${USER}, %USERNAME%) are judged in place like bracketed ones, and /home/${USER}/workspace/repo is no longer refused. (2) The home-username boundary now accepts any character outside the segment-name class and the separators, so a tilde path written straight after a ], ) or ; that ends a host-path match still refuses. value.author: orchestrator
value.text: Round after merging main (#215): two CodeRabbit findings fixed. (1) The email-address domain pattern backtracked quadratically on a long final label followed by '.1' (1,282 ms at 16k letters, 4x per doubling; 18.7 s at 64k). The cause was [A-Za-z]{2,} overlapping the [A-Za-z0-9-]* after it under a failing boundary lookahead. CodeRabbit's suggested non-empty labels stayed quadratic and dropped empty-label addresses (fail-open; a 300k-case fuzz showed 6,455 differences). The rewrite is one [A-Za-z0-9.-] character, then dot-delimited [A-Za-z0-9-]* labels, then [A-Za-z]{2}[A-Za-z0-9-]*: the same language (300k structured fuzz cases, 41,179 with matches, 0 differences) in linear time (64k-character lines in about 2 ms). (2) PATH_NAME_CHARACTER now includes \p{M}, and the segment loop judges whole code points, so a decomposed accent or an astral letter no longer refuses a placeholder home's subdirectory; an astral symbol (emoji) stays a delimiter. New corpus rows: two must-allow (combining mark, astral letter) and two must-refuse (root path after an astral symbol, empty email label). New mutations no-combining-marks, code-unit-name-scan and nonempty-email-labels each flip exactly their row, and all 33 mutations pass. New test: the email scan stays under 200 ms on 64k-character lines, and it fails with the old pattern (18.7 s). Gates: typecheck, lint, docstring, duplication and privacy pass; gate suites 140/140 under Node, 11/11 under Bun.

value.text: Review round on ba811b8 (3 CodeRabbit + 2 Sourcery findings), all fixed. (1) Sourcery High: issue #193 requires preserving refusal of concrete process details, and its own example was praised for having 'no … concrete PID'. The gate now refuses /proc/<digits>/…: proc-digits and proc-digits-root-entry moved to must-refuse, and the root-entry exemption is self-only. /proc, /proc/self/… and /proc/<placeholder>/… stay allowed. The new mutation allow-numeric-pid flips exactly proc-digits. No fleet tracker contains a numeric procfs path. (2) Sourcery Medium: new must-allow row proc-trailing-slash (/proc/). (3) CodeRabbit Major: the proof CLI child no longer inherits NODE_V8_COVERAGE or NODE_TEST_CONTEXT, so its disposable mutants stay out of c8's raw data. (4) CodeRabbit Minor: the README states the tilde boundary exactly (any character other than a letter, number, . _ ~ - / or backslash) and no longer lists numeric pids among the allowed procfs forms. (5) CodeRabbit Minor: the evidence doc counts are current (61 must-allow, 83 must-refuse, 34 mutations), its mutation table is regenerated from the proof output, and a sixth-round summary was added. Gates: all 34 mutations ok; typecheck, lint, docstring, duplication and privacy pass; gate suites 140/140 under Node and 15/15 under Bun.

value.text: CodeRabbit on 3c13975: the no-echo assertion compared raw path tokens with JSON.stringify(report). JSON doubles backslashes, so an echoed Windows path could never match: five must-refuse rows were effectively unchecked. Tokens are now compared in their JSON-escaped form. A Windows self-check proves that the raw token is invisible in JSON and the escaped one is detected. gate-public-forms passes 11/11 under Node and Bun; typecheck, lint, duplication and privacy pass.
